title: Reference approach: PyTorch Vision Studio
approach: Build PyTorch Vision Studio in small milestones. Implement: Document dataset, licenses, provenance, and preprocessing; Compare a baseline and justified architecture; Track training/validation metrics and perform error analysis; Save reproducible checkpoints and safe restoration steps; Validate image inputs and provide useful error messages; Write unit and end-to-end tests; Optionally optimize or export on a supported target; Document intended use, limitations, and setup; Provide a minimal API or UI for image prediction. Use synthetic data while developing, choose a documented dataset for the final experiment, and keep train/validation/test splits separate.

reference_snippets.code:
import torch
from torch import nn
model = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(8, 16), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(16, 2)).eval()
with torch.inference_mode():
    output = model(torch.zeros(1, 8))
assert output.shape == (1, 2)
print("smoke test passed")

review_notes: This is a protected teaching outline, not a claim that a trained artifact is included.
Benchmark the actual target hardware and report uncertainty.
Review data licensing, privacy, bias, and intended-use constraints.
